content.text: Purpose
Create, change, copy, or disable an agent from a persona, a system prompt template, and a tool_policy, in four phases: Understand, Propose, Write, Hand-Off.

Conventions: Load only the sections of the 'Agent-Building Conventions' resource this playbook needs — before Phase 2 (Propose), in one call: fetch_resource(resource_id, block_ids=["res-conv-h-policy", "res-conv-h-memory"]). A heading anchor returns its whole section; the resource_id is in this playbook's links (linked_blocks). Only when needed: res-conv-h-templates when you author or change a template; res-conv-h-managed on a 409.
Identify the mode

Create: a new agent (create_agent). Update: change the config in place (update_agent). Copy: a variant of an activatable agent (copy_agent). Disable / Reactivate: update_agent with status, not transition_*.
Create Mode
Phase 1 — Understand
The persona must exist and have an active version.
Check with get_persona(identifier). If it's missing, create it first via the "Create & Maintain Persona" playbook and come back. The order is always persona → template → agent.
Clarify the agent name: short and unambiguous (display name in the list).

Choose a template: Does an existing one fit (list_system_prompts, with locale per template — prefer the target language)? If so, note its system_prompt_template_id. Only if none fits, author a new one as a draft and submit it for review, following section res-conv-h-templates — by default tools-overview does NOT belong in the template.
Clarify permissions: Should the agent only read, or also write? This determines the tool_policy (sections res-conv-h-policy and res-conv-h-memory).
Phase 2 — Propose
Present the planned configuration to the user: name, persona, template, and tool_policy (read scopes and write capabilities in plain language).
Explain the consequences (with an active persona and a template the agent is activatable and can start enabled right away) and get confirmation before you write.
Phase 3 — Write
Call create_agent with
name
persona_id
(persona with an active version),
system_prompt_template_id
, and
tool_policy
. Without a tool_policy the default applies: read everything, write nothing.
status
defaults to disabled; set enabled only if the agent is activatable — otherwise the server responds with 409.
Phase 4 — Hand-Off

Verify with get_agent(agent_id): missing=[] and activatable=true; plus get_persona → body_rendered with no unresolved placeholders. You don't check the rendered prompt (fetch_agent returns 404 for other agents); the target agent's first start does.
Report name, ID, and status back and name any open gaps (missing). At the end, offer a consistency & drift check.
Update Mode
Understand: get_agent(agent_id) reads persona, template, tool_policy, status, and missing; list_agents finds the ID.
Propose: Show exactly the delta — which field changes and why. Only the specified fields get overwritten; an omitted tool_policy stays unchanged.
Write: update_agent with the changed fields. A set
tool_policy replaces the policy entirely
(replace semantics) — carry over the existing values that should stay.
Hand-Off: get_agent again (missing empty, status correct). Running sessions need a new session for the change to take effect.
Copy Mode
Only activatable agents can be copied; check this beforehand with get_agent (activatable).
Call copy_agent with the source ID.
name
is optional (otherwise "<Name> (Copy)"). The copy takes over persona, template, description, and status.
Adjust the copy via update_agent (e.g., a tighter tool_policy) and verify with get_agent.
Disable & Reactivate

There is only enabled and disabled, both via update_agent(status=...). A disabled agent is filtered out of the list and its render endpoint responds with 409. Before disabling, check whether the agent is still in use and warn the user. Reactivating is only possible as long as the agent stays activatable.
Activatability (activatable)

An agent is activatable when persona AND template are set AND the persona has an active version. missing lists the gaps in stable order (persona, template, persona_active); empty means activatable. If persona or template is missing, the agent is a shell (is_shell): allowed, but not renderable and not copyable; complete it later via update_agent.
Pitfalls
get_agent reads the config of ANY agent in the workspace; fetch_agent (rendered prompt) only works for your OWN agent.
Permissions:
create_agent, update_agent, and copy_agent require agent_write, writing templates requires system_prompt_write; transition_system_prompt only goes from draft to review.
Not available:
activating a template (ADR-0040, a human does that in the web UI), deleting an agent (ADR-0030), and transition_* on agents (no versions, changes are config updates).
Anti-Patterns
Creating an agent with status=enabled even though it isn't activatable — the server rejects with 409.
Wiring up a persona without an active version — the agent stays non-activatable (missing lists persona_active).
Sending only a partial tool_policy on update, assuming the rest would be preserved — it is replaced entirely.

Setting write capabilities more generously than the task needs instead of following the tool policy pattern (res-conv-h-policy: secure by default, minimal capabilities, promote_retire only for genuine switching needs).
Not verifying with get_agent after create_agent or update_agent — an incomplete shell would go unnoticed. A 404 from fetch_agent for an OTHER agent, on the other hand, is expected.
